bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42521522 (hdf5): Heap-buffer-overflow READ 1 found by fuzz target h5_read_fuzzer [asan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/42521522
bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json / reproduction_report.json / sanitizer_trace.txt / default_crash_trace.txt / patch.diff / staged vulnerable source in container gt-arvo_42521522-workspace:/src/hdf5 / /src/h5_read_fuzzer.c / staged poc
bug_description.normalized: The exact staged 2823-byte witness with SHA-256 `3132140d17a24deb811b05f8b7c0c2b2b2217648f22c50b4bd1c90b6e43071fa` is a raw `h5_read_fuzzer` corpus entry, not the file bytes HDF5 parses directly: `h5_read_fuzzer` drops raw byte 0 and writes the remaining 2822 bytes to a temporary file before calling `H5Fopen()`. In that written file, `H5FD_locate_signature()` finds the HDF5 signature at parsed-file offset `0`, so `H5F__superblock_prefix_decode()` reads a legacy superblock with `super_vers == 0`, `sizeof_addr == 2`, and `sizeof_size == 4`. `H5F__cache_superblock_deserialize()` then decodes the legacy 4-byte status word `01 1a ff ff` as `status_flags == 0xffff1a01`, but vulnerable code only debug-asserts `status_flags <= 255` and truncates it to `sblock->status_flags == 0x01` instead of rejecting the malformed superblock. The same accepted superblock decodes a cached-STAB root symbol-table entry with `header == 0x00ff`, and `H5F__super_read()` rebases `base_addr` to the located `super_addr == 0`, so that relative root-object address resolves to parsed-file offset `0x00ff` (raw offset `0x0100`), where the witness contains `OHDR 02 3f ...`. `H5O__prefix_deserialize()` reads that version-2 object-header prefix, decodes the 8-byte chunk-0 size bytes `dd ff ff ff ff ff ff ff` as `udata->chunk0_size == 0xffffffffffffffdd`, and `H5O__cache_get_final_load_size()` adds the 38-byte prefix size, wrapping unsigned `size_t actual_len` to `3`. Stage 01's saved allocation context confirms that `H5C__load_entry()` then shrinks the root object-header image to a 3-byte heap region. Because the parsed object-header version is not 1, `H5O__cache_verify_chksum()` still calls `H5F_get_checksums(image, 3, ...)`; `chk_p = buf + 3 - 4` therefore underflows to `buf - 1`, and `UINT32DECODE(chk_p, *s_chksum)` produces the saved AddressSanitizer heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 1 at `src/H5Fio.c:556`. The patch hardens superblock and driver-info deserialization; for this exact witness, the added `if (status_flags > 255) HGOTO_ERROR(...)` in `H5F__cache_superblock_deserialize()` blocks the malformed legacy superblock before the downstream object-header length wrap.

source.description: Source. This is the first HDF5 parser statement that materializes vulnerability-relevant state after signature admission.
source.value_from: The raw 2823-byte corpus entry is not parsed directly: `h5_read_fuzzer` drops raw byte 0 and writes raw offsets `1..2822` as the temporary file. `H5FD_locate_signature()` admits that written file at parsed-file offset `0`, so after the 8-byte signature this statement reads parsed-file offset `8` / raw offset `9`, whose value is `0x00`, into `sblock->super_vers`.
source.note: The libFuzzer entry point is only the unscored harness boundary. The vulnerability-relevant parser state begins here, inside HDF5's superblock reader.

root_cause.description: Root cause. The legacy superblock parser accepts a 4-byte status word whose high bytes are nonzero because the only range check is a debug-only `HDassert`. In release builds the malformed 32-bit value is truncated to one byte and parsing continues on attacker-controlled legacy superblock state that should have been rejected.
root_cause.note: On the exact written-file witness these four bytes are `01 1a ff ff`, so `status_flags == 0xffff1a01` but `sblock->status_flags` becomes `0x01`. The fix replaces the assertion-only invariant with `if (status_flags > 255) HGOTO_ERROR(...)` at this exact site.

sink.description: ASan sink. After the object-header image length has wrapped down to 3 bytes, decoding the stored 4-byte checksum dereferences `chk_p == buf - 1` and reads one byte before the heap allocation.
sink.note: Stage 01's saved AddressSanitizer trace reports `heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 1` at this exact line and says the faulting address is `1 bytes to the left of 3-byte region [0x602000003950,0x602000003953)` allocated in `H5C__load_entry`.

tainted_value_origin.description: The root object's chunk-0 length field is the critical attacker-controlled numeric value that later wraps the object-header image length to 3.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: After the malformed legacy superblock and base-address rebase direct HDF5 to the root object at parsed-file offset `0x00ff` (raw offset `0x0100`), the version-2 object-header prefix stores the eight chunk-size bytes `dd ff ff ff ff ff ff ff` at parsed-file offsets `0x0119..0x0120` (raw offsets `0x011a..0x0121`). This statement decodes them as `udata->chunk0_size == 0xffffffffffffffdd`.
tainted_value_origin.note: With the same `flags == 0x3f` prefix, `H5O_SIZEOF_HDR(udata->oh)` is 38 on this path, so the next size addition wraps to 3.

parser_admitted.description: After `h5_read_fuzzer` drops raw byte 0 and writes the remaining 2822 bytes to disk, HDF5 finds the signature in that written file at parsed-file offset 0 and records `super_addr == 0`.
parser_admitted.note: `H5FD_locate_signature()` checks address 0 first (`addr = 0` when `n == 8`) before trying higher power-of-two offsets, so this is the format-admission checkpoint that fixes all downstream parsed-file offsets. Raw-input offsets are therefore one byte larger than the parsed-file offsets cited below.

evidence_limitations: `run_flags.json` sets `runtime_disambiguation` to `false`, so Stage 02 did not add instrumentation. The chain is closed from the staged source, the staged witness bytes, and the saved Stage 01 crash/allocation traces only.

The staged vulnerable checkout available here is container-local at `gt-arvo_42521522-workspace:/src/hdf5` on commit `ea5b3952f71ae613830ece0a4416656ecacf070d`, not the metadata `vulnerable_commit` `bd7616cf98ae52e77f710a16fb4d334be3cb5ce9`. The line anchors below are therefore resolved against the staged container source that produced the saved sanitizer trace.
Because `h5_read_fuzzer` drops the first raw byte before writing the temporary file, the notes below default to parsed-file offsets unless a raw-input offset is explicitly called out.

coarse_trace.summary: The raw corpus entry is turned into a temporary file by dropping the first byte, HDF5 finds the signature at parsed-file offset 0, and the legacy superblock parser accepts a malformed 4-byte status word instead of rejecting it.

The accepted superblock decodes a cached-STAB root entry with `root_addr == 0x00ff`, and rebasing `base_addr` to `super_addr == 0` makes that relative address resolve to parsed-file offset `0x00ff` (raw offset `0x0100`).
Root-group initialization follows the cached-STAB path into the root object header at offset `0x00ff`, where the witness provides `OHDR 02 3f` and an 8-byte `chunk0_size == 0xffffffffffffffdd`.

Adding the 38-byte version-2 object-header prefix size to that attacker-controlled chunk length wraps unsigned `size_t actual_len` to `3`, and the metadata cache reallocates the object-header image to the same 3-byte heap region later named by ASan.

Because the parsed object header is not version 1, checksum verification still runs on the 3-byte image; the stored-checksum pointer underflows to `buf - 1`, and `UINT32DECODE` performs the saved one-byte heap-buffer-overflow read.

fine_trace.note: Source step. After the parser-admitted checkpoint has established the signature at parsed-file offset `0`, this statement reads the version byte at parsed-file offset `8` / raw offset `9` and materializes `super_vers == 0`.
Because `super_vers == 0`, the legacy-prefix path reads the width fields from the old-format locations. On the exact witness these bytes make `sizeof_addr == 2` and `sizeof_size == 4`.

Root-cause step. The legacy superblock's four status bytes `01 1a ff ff` decode as `status_flags == 0xffff1a01`; in release builds the only check is the debug-only `HDassert`, so the code truncates this to `sblock->status_flags == 0x01` and `UINT32DECODE` leaves `image` positioned at the following address fields instead of rejecting the malformed superblock.

With `image` already advanced past the malformed 4-byte status word in step 3 and `H5F_SIZEOF_ADDR(f) == 2`, the next eight bytes decode to `base_addr == HADDR_UNDEF` (`ff ff`), `ext_addr == HADDR_UNDEF`, `stored_eof == 0x0b05`, and `driver_addr == 0x9bff`. These decodes advance `image` to the start of the root symbol-table entry.
The root symbol-table entry bytes are interpreted with the same legacy widths. On the exact witness this decode yields `ent->header == 0x00ff` and `ent->type == 1`, i.e. `H5G_CACHED_STAB`.
The attacker-controlled root-entry header address becomes the file's root object location: `sblock->root_addr == 0x00ff`.

The parser-admitted checkpoint already fixed `super_addr == 0`. Because the decoded `base_addr` from step 4 is not that value, this branch rebases `sblock->base_addr` to `0`. After that rebase, the relative root-object address from step 6 resolves to parsed-file offset `0x00ff` (raw offset `0x0100`).
Root-group initialization carries the rebased root address into the object-location struct, so the next metadata lookup targets the root object at parsed-file offset `0x00ff`.
Because the cached root entry type from step 5 is `H5G_CACHED_STAB`, `H5G_mkroot()` asks `H5O_msg_exists()` to inspect the root object header.

At parsed-file offset `0x00ff` (raw offset `0x0100`), the witness bytes begin `OHDR 02 3f`. This deserializer therefore materializes `oh->version == 2` and `oh->flags == 0x3f`, selecting the checksum-bearing version-2 object-header format with every optional prefix field present.
Because `oh->flags & H5O_HDR_CHUNK0_SIZE` selects the 8-byte case, the next eight bytes `dd ff ff ff ff ff ff ff` decode to `udata->chunk0_size == 0xffffffffffffffdd`.
With `udata->chunk0_size == 0xffffffffffffffdd` from step 11 and `H5O_SIZEOF_HDR(udata->oh) == 38` from step 10's version-2 flags, this unsigned addition wraps modulo `2^64` to `*actual_len == 3`.

The metadata cache commits to the wrapped size from step 12 and shrinks the root object-header image to `actual_len == 3`. Stage 01's saved allocation context names this exact line and reports the resulting heap region as `[0x602000003950,0x602000003953)`.

The object header parsed in step 10 is version 2, so checksum verification is not skipped. `H5C__load_entry()` passes the 3-byte image length from step 13 into this callback as `len`, and the callback forwards that same length into `H5F_get_checksums()`.
With `buf_size == 3` from step 14 and `H5_SIZEOF_CHKSUM == 4`, this pointer computation underflows to `chk_p == buf - 1` before any checksum bytes are decoded.

Sink step. The first byte fetched by `UINT32DECODE` comes from `chk_p == buf - 1`, so the stored-checksum decode reads one byte to the left of the 3-byte heap allocation from step 13. This is the exact AddressSanitizer crash site.

sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves_note: The staged fix hardens `src/H5Fsuper_cache.c`. For this exact witness, the new `if (status_flags > 255)` check in the legacy superblock path rejects the malformed `01 1a ff ff` status word before the cached root entry can drive the wrapped 3-byte object-header length into checksum verification. Stage 02 did not execute the fixed image; this is a source-level conclusion from the staged diff and the witnessed bytes.
sanitizer_ground_truth.crash_summary: AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 1 in H5F_get_checksums at src/H5Fio.c:556 while H5O__cache_verify_chksum validated a root object-header image that had been shrunk to 3 bytes by H5C__load_entry.

cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: Yes. Steps 10-13 decode the root object's `chunk0_size == 0xffffffffffffffdd`, show the unsigned wrap to `actual_len == 3`, and land on the exact `H5C__load_entry` reallocation line named by the saved allocation context before steps 14-16 consume that same 3-byte image at the ASan sink.
cross_validation.trace_consistent_with_stack: Yes. The saved project stack is `H5F_get_checksums -> H5O__cache_verify_chksum -> H5C__load_entry -> H5O_msg_exists -> H5G_mkroot -> H5F_open`, and the fine trace refines that same path with the earlier legacy-superblock acceptance, base-address rebase, root-entry propagation, and object-header size-wrap steps that make the sink reachable.

poc.trigger: Stage 01's authoritative vulnerable run executed `PYTHONPATH=gt_generation python3 -m gt_toolkit arvo-workspace --result-dir /mnt/datastore/gt_generation/gt_results/arvo_42521522 run --version vulnerable --expect crash`, fed the staged raw `poc` corpus entry to `/out/h5_read_fuzzer`, and reproduced `AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 1` in `H5F_get_checksums` with stack `H5O__cache_verify_chksum -> H5C__load_entry -> H5O_msg_exists -> H5G_mkroot`.

format.name: h5_read_fuzzer corpus entry
format.contract: Exactly the staged 2823-byte raw corpus entry stored at `gt_results/arvo_42521522/poc` (SHA-256 `3132140d17a24deb811b05f8b7c0c2b2b2217648f22c50b4bd1c90b6e43071fa`). `h5_read_fuzzer` consumes byte 0 as `decider`, decrements `size`, advances `data`, and writes the remaining 2822 bytes to the temporary file passed to `H5Fopen`; the source-grounded trigger semantics below are about that written file, not about the raw corpus bytes at the same offsets. For this exact witness, the written file begins with the HDF5 signature at parsed-file offset `0`; its legacy superblock decodes `super_vers == 0`, `sizeof_addr == 2`, `sizeof_size == 4`, and `status_flags == 0xffff1a01`; its cached-STAB root entry has relative `root_addr == 0x00ff`; and the root object header at parsed-file offset `0x00ff` (raw offset `0x0100`) begins `OHDR 02 3f` and carries chunk-0 size bytes `dd ff ff ff ff ff ff ff` at parsed-file offsets `0x0119..0x0120` (raw offsets `0x011a..0x0121`), which wrap `actual_len` to 3 before checksum verification. Stage 02 does not generalize this witness beyond those exact demonstrated bytes and state transitions.
